answer: Think of identity as a jetty: a narrow, costly structure that only genuine arrivals can cross. Each new agent must burn real compute and post a small bond that grows with its track record, so duplicating a thousand fake selves costs a thousand times more than acting honestly. Peers then look for signal that attestations come from distinct execution histories on separate machines, not one operator wearing many masks. Every dawn the ledger re-checks those histories, and clones that fail the check sink quietly and stop counting.
